paper_metadata.title: Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging of Acute Infarction: Comparison with Routine Diffusion and Follow-up MR Imaging

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study clearly defines the target population, recruitment period, and setting. Inclusion and exclusion criteria are explicit, and the sample is described with key baseline characteristics. The use of consecutive recruitment helps limit selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Forty consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke were recruited between July 2015 and January 2017.
items.reasoning: The source is defined as consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke at a specific hospital center.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Forty consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke were recruited between July 2015 and January 2017.
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment is a standard method to minimize selection bias in prognostic studies.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between July 2015 and January 2017.
items.reasoning: The dates are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Tianjin First Central Hospital, Tianjin, China
items.reasoning: The hospital and city are provided in the author affiliations and study context.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The inclusion criteria were (a) adult, at least 20 years old; (b) clear onset time of stroke attack; (c) the first MR imaging examination within 24 hours after symptom onset; (d) follow-up MR imaging 1 month later; (e) clinical National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale scores... Exclusion criteria were (a) MR imaging contraindications... (c) thrombolytic therapy...
items.reasoning: Criteria are detailed and include 'zero time' (within 24 hours of onset).

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Forty consecutive patients... 37 patients... were included in the data analysis.
items.reasoning: 37 out of 40 eligible patients were analyzed (92.5% participation rate), which is well above the 80% threshold.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1: M/F 28/9, Age (y) 58.4 ± 8.4, First MR imaging examination after stroke onset (h) 13.6 ± 5.1, NIHSS at admission 4.8 ± 3.7.
items.reasoning: Key prognostic variables like age, sex, time to imaging, and baseline severity (NIHSS) are reported.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for all patients from recruitment to analysis. Only 3 patients were excluded for specific, non-informative reasons (motion and therapy change), and the follow-up rate for the final cohort was 100%.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis

items.evidence_snippet: Forty consecutive patients... 37 patients... were included in the data analysis.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out

items.evidence_snippet: Two patients were excluded for head motion and one for thrombolytic therapy

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (DKI and DWI metrics) are measured using standardized, objective MR protocols. The methods are described in detail, and measurements were performed by multiple blinded/independent readers.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: DKI was measured by using multiband diffusion echo-planar imaging sequences with three b values of 0, 1000, and 2000 sec/mm2; 20 diffusion directions... ADC maps were calculated from the standard DWI postprocessing routines.
items.reasoning: The technical parameters for the prognostic factors (ADC, MD, MK) are explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Signal measurements, volume outlines, and lesion counting were independently assessed by two radiologists... The results were reviewed by a third radiologist
items.reasoning: The use of two independent readers and a senior reviewer ensures high reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: For large lesions (maximal diameter ≥ 1 cm)... for lesions with maximal diameter of less than 1 cm, we defined them as small lesions.
items.reasoning: The 1cm cut-off is a standard clinical threshold and not derived from the data itself.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All imaging examinations were performed by using a 3-T Siemens Trio imager
items.reasoning: A single scanner and protocol were used for all participants.

items.evidence_snippet: 37 patients... were included in the data analysis.
